limits: One checkpoint, one 600-item C-Eval validation slice, one run per protocol.
36.2% is well below published C-Eval scores for this model class; model size is the first suspect but this run does not test it.
The shuffle check ran on 200 of the 600 questions, so its interval is wider than the headline one.
Likelihood scoring removes the letter slot, not every ordering effect: a 15% residual spread remains and is not explained here.

scorings.acc_norm: the same sum divided by the option's token count
scorings.loglikelihood: sum log P(option tokens | question + all options + 答案：)

protocol.why: the published protocol reads four letter logits and takes the argmax; on this checkpoint that reads the option's slot rather than its content, so the same model scores below a constant-answer baseline. Scoring each option's own likelihood clears it.

shuffle_check.note: the same questions with the four options permuted by a fixed seed; a scorer that reads the option slot would move far more than 1.5 points
